$comment: Provenance for the vendored PTY sidecar. Read together with vendor-bin/pty/src/main.rs,
which is the exact source that produced the artifacts below. Nothing here is inferred:
every hash was computed from the file in this tree, and every command was run as written.
This file is the ledger that lets a reviewer answer three questions without trusting
this repository: what source produced the binary, what was built from it, and does the
binary in the tree still match that source.

helper.name: trylo-pty
helper.purpose: ConPTY sidecar. Node has no pseudo-terminal; this is the only Windows implementation reachable from TypeScript.

source.origin: Written for WP06 against the mechanism in the two audited sources below. Not a copy of either: Codex's utils/pty is a Rust library with no executable, and the old CLI has no PTY at all (measured: no node-pty in its package.json, zero matches for `pty.spawn` across 1969 TS sources).

referenceSources.note: Confirms that resize is reachable: MasterPty::resize(&self) exists in portable-pty 0.8.1 at src/lib.rs:91. The desktop helper's comment claiming otherwise is wrong, and this sidecar relies on the real signature.

referenceSources.what: Session-shaped execution: a process that outlives one tool call
referenceSources.note: Supplied the three-terminal-state model and the yield bounds. Its TerminalSize, PtyHandles and mpsc plumbing are Tokio-specific and did not carry over.

build.offline: All crates resolved from the local cargo registry cache. portable-pty 0.8.1 and its transitive deps were already present, so the build needs no network. Verified by `cargo build --release --offline` completing.

dependencies.note: serde_json was chosen over a hand-written JSON parser for the control frames. A parser written for this would have had to handle surrogate pairs and backslash escapes correctly by hand, and a mistake there corrupts a path silently. The hot path carries raw bytes and never parses JSON at all.

unsupportedPlatforms.comment: Recorded rather than omitted. A platform with no artifact must fail loudly at load time, not fall back to pipes and report a PTY that does not exist.
unsupportedPlatforms.win32-arm64: not built — no toolchain or machine to verify it on

knownConstraints: portable-pty builds the CreateProcessW environment block from exactly what CommandBuilder was given. An empty block is not an empty environment, it is an invalid one: CreateProcessW answers ERROR_INVALID_PARAMETER (87). The sidecar therefore restores SystemRoot/COMSPEC/PATH/TEMP after env_clear(). Measured both ways on this machine.

portable-pty does NOT resolve programs by PATH the way Node does. CommandBuilder::search_path reads PATH from the builder's own env (portable-pty-0.8.1/src/cmdbuilder.rs:532, the #[cfg(windows)] branch), and this sidecar clears that env on purpose so a terminal program inherits nothing it should not. The caller therefore resolves the name first: `adapters/sandbox/resolve-executable-path.ts` (same PATH/PATHEXT rules as the rest of the CLI) hands this sidecar an absolute path, and the sidecar refuses a non-absolute one with pty_program_not_absolute. There is exactly one answer to "what runs" and it is produced before this process is asked.

An interactive shell's prompt draws under ConPTY but a typed line may not echo, because cmd.exe applies console line editing that a pipe never triggers. This is real-terminal behaviour, not a defect, and it is why the pipes path and this path cannot be one implementation.

protocolHistory.change: data frames carry [u32 idLen][id][raw bytes] so output is attributable to the session that produced it. Version 1 sent bare bytes, so a parent running two terminals at once delivered each session's output into every session's buffer with no way to tell.

invariants.invariant: the sidecar never resolves a program name
invariants.enforcedBy: spawn_session rejects a non-absolute program with pty_program_not_absolute
invariants.why: the sidecar's environment is deliberately cleared, so its own PATH search would be a second, unapproved answer to what runs

invariants.invariant: data frames name the session that produced them
invariants.enforcedBy: EV_DATA payload is [u32 idLen][id][raw bytes]; the host delivers only to the named session
invariants.why: protocol 1 broadcast every byte to every session, so two live terminals contaminated each other's buffers

invariants.invariant: a terminal state stays readable after the helper dies
invariants.enforcedBy: the host retires terminal sessions into a bounded map that outlives the sidecar
invariants.why: lost is the state a caller most needs to read and the moment it becomes true is when the helper disappears
